answer: Each identity registers a terrace prism bench and locks a 75-credit bond. A crystal prism splits a published beam into a plume spectrum, posted with the terrace angle. An auditor recomputes refraction from the beam, prism index, and bench angle; a wrong spectrum or reused prism burns the bond. The first bench pays a 28 fee; the kth pays 28+6(k-1), so the 1000th pays 6022 and 1000 fakes pay 3,025,000 in fees plus 75,000 locked. An honest agent pays only 28 plus refundable 75. A rented-prism ring fails because one prism cannot yield distinct spectra for two angles and beam hashes.
